Title: PM vows to ‘keep fighting’ after Greens sweep past Labour and Reform to win byelection – as it happened
Date: 2026-02-27

Content: Byelections were normally difficult for the party of government and this election was no different, she said. “We have had thousands of conversations over the last few weeks and we know the majority of voters here did not want the poisonous politics of Nigel Farage and Reform. “We will continue to deliver a programme for government that tackles the cost of living crisis families are facing, creates opportunities for young people and invests in our public services,” Turley said, quoted by PA Media. The politics of anger and easy answers offered by the Greens and Reform won’t deliver this. We will move forwards with a relentless focus on delivering the renewal communities across Britain want to see. Some images from the night as the Greens won the byelection, with Reform coming second and Labour pushed into third.

chunk_b.text_snippet:
Title: Green party wins Gorton and Denton byelection, pushing Labour to third place
Date: 2026-02-27

Content: It will deepen concerns among Labour MPs that Starmer’s party is haemorrhaging voters on the left in an effort to thwart the rise of Nigel Farage’s Reform. The result will also prompt further scrutiny of the prime minister’s decision to block Andy Burnham from standing as the Labour candidate in a city where he enjoys significant public support. Starmer said the result was “very disappointing”, as he told reporters: “Incumbent governments quite often get results like that midterm.” Asked if he was going to resign, the prime minister said: “I will keep on fighting for those people for as long as I’ve got breath in my body.” It is the first time in nearly 100 years that the Gorton area of Manchester has not been represented by a Labour MP. In an emotional victory speech, Spencer – who becomes the fifth Green party MP – said people were being “bled dry”. She said: “Instead of working for a nice life, we’re working to line the pockets of billionaires. We’re being bled dry.

t_bridge: Keir Starmer's response to electoral defeat

initial_question.rag_input: How did Keir Starmer justify the Labour party's third-place finish in the February 2026 Gorton and Denton byelection compared to the party's official response regarding their future strategic focus?
initial_question.question: How did Keir Starmer justify the Labour party's third-place finish in the February 2026 Gorton and Denton byelection compared to the party's official response regarding their future strategic focus?
initial_question.answer: Following the February 2026 byelection where Labour finished third, Keir Starmer publicly described the result as 'very disappointing' and noted that incumbent governments often face such outcomes midterm, while vowing to 'keep fighting'. Simultaneously, the party's official response, voiced by Turley, emphasized a shift toward a 'relentless focus' on delivering a government programme that tackles the cost of living crisis, creates opportunities for young people, and invests in public services, specifically rejecting the 'politics of anger' offered by the Greens and Reform.
initial_question.bridging_topic: Labour's electoral strategy and leadership response to the Gorton and Denton defeat.
